jon: Heads-up — replay harness replay-27 shows ~18% p95 regression in JSON-mode toolcalls vs our synthetic baseline. p50 48ms -> 52ms, p95 160ms -> 190ms, tokens/s down ~9%.

maria: Which config did you replay with? dynamic batching on? JSON validation enabled?

jon: replay-27 config attached (ran on dedicated-staging pool). Structured/json mode = true, validate_json = true, funcall = enabled. Batching: max_batch_ms=8, max_batch_tokens=2048, min_batch_size=1.

jon: Profiler top hot paths (sample):
```
kernelselect.select_kernel  34%\ncontinuous_batcher.emit     18%\nkv_cache.lookup             12%\njson_validator.validate     9%\ngpu_compute.matmul          7%\n```

perf-bot: replay-27 finished: p95=190ms (+30ms vs baseline), KV cache miss rate 6.8% (+4.1pp), small-batch ratio 37%. Full logs: https://ci/replays/replay-27.log

arik: Do we have a comparison of small-batch ratio vs synthetic? 37% small batches seems high. Could be batching heuristic selecting a low-overhead kernel causing extra memcpy.

jon: Synthetic run (same seed but without session churn) small-batch ratio 12% and p95 160ms. So the replay mixes a lot of short sessions and toolcalls.

kevin: KV pattern note: structured toolcalls add longer function names + metadata -> KV keys larger and more frequent eviction. Quick check from the log: `go run tools/kv_hist.go replay-27.log | head` shows many 64-128B keys vs usual 32B.

maria: I reproduced locally: run the replay harness with `--session-mix=high-churn` and same model/weights => p95 regressed ~20%. Synthetic (steady sessions) didn't regress. So it's clearly workload distribution dependent.

jon: Hypothesis: kernelselect currently optimizes for average seq length; with high churn we see more short sequences and kernelselect picks a small-kernel path that interacts poorly with KV cache and with JSON validation flow, causing CPU pre/post work to dominate. We should try a seq-aware kernelselect policy and an experiment flipping `kernelselect.policy=prefer_large_matmul_for_funcalls=true`.

arik: I'll run a couple experiments on staging. Experiment plan: 1) toggle kernelselect to seq-aware; 2) increase max_batch_ms to 12 to allow more coalescing; 3) run with and without json validation. I'll report p50/p95 + kv miss.

perf-qa-bot: Quick micro-experiments (local):
- disabling JSON validation reduced p95 by ~12ms but caused validation error rate -> retries 1.2x (toolcall retries due to schema mismatch).
- enabling lazy-json-validate (only validate final object) reduced CPU by ~7ms with 0.2% extra failures.

jon: We can't wholesale disable validation in prod. Data integrity is important. But lazy/partial validation sounds promising. Can we implement a windowed validator that checks only the final 512-token window?

kevin: Draft optimization (pseudo):
```
func lazyValidate(stream) bool {
  buf := ring.LastN(stream, 512)
  return jsonschema.Validate(buf)
}
```
This should cut CPU while preserving most catches.

maria: Also suggest adding a small adaptive backoff for retries to smooth KV pressure. Many quick retries are hammering KV and causing evictions. Eg backoff: 10ms + jitter * attempts.

jon: Agreed. Also need apples-to-apples: use the same replayer seed across experiments and run each experiment for >=30m to converge the KV steady state. We'll run on dedicated capacity at 2k rps to match production.'

arik: Running first batch now (kernelselect=seq-aware, max_batch_ms=12). Kickoff: 2026-03-17T23:05Z. I'll post results in this thread.

perf-bot: experiment-run:exp-901 started (staging-dedicated).

sre-bot: Note: watch GPU memory fragmentation when increasing batch_ms; set oom fallback policy to `spill_to_cpu` in case.

jon: I'll open a bench plan doc and tracker ticket with acceptance criteria: p95 within 5% of baseline and KV miss delta < 1pp. Ownership: jon (plan), arik (kernelselect runs), kevin (kv hist + lazy-validate patch), maria (replay harness).

kevin: I'll prototype lazy validator and add opt-in flag `json.lazy_validate=true` for canary.

maria: :thumbsup:

jon: thanks — we'll reconvene after run results. If anyone sees an obvious quick win (eg bump batch_ms to 15) please try on a small run first.
